aboutGame.title: What is Drop Command?
paragraphs: Drop Command is a tactical sci-fi strategy game built around off-map deployment. Instead of walking units through a doorway, you call mechs, tanks, infantry, VTOLs, and battle armour directly onto a landing zone you choose, spending a limited tonnage budget, a cooldown, and a delay timer to change the shape of a fight.

Every match turns on the same decisions: read the board, pick a safe landing point, match the payload to the problem, and keep roughly a third of your allowance in reserve for the push you have not seen yet. Our wiki covers unit roles, mech builds, campaign planning, mission tactics, controls, and updates so new commanders and veterans can drop with a plan.

modules.name: Drop Command Beginner Guide
modules.description: A beginner-friendly guide covering the core gameplay loop, battlefield controls, campaign basics, and first mission strategies. It helps new players understand mech piloting, squad management, and how to start building their space empire.

highlights.detail: Locate the command prompt, drop menu, or hotkey your game uses for deployment.
Confirm the prefix, keybind, or call-in button before the fight starts.
Select the target: the item, unit, or landing zone you want to affect.
Set the quantity or tonnage and start with the smallest useful payload.
Watch the arrival and confirm exactly where the payload lands.
Write down the working command so you can repeat it under pressure.

modules.name: Drop Command Units Guide
modules.description: A complete overview of playable units including Mechs, Tanks, Infantry, VTOLs, and Battle Armour. This module explains unit roles, strengths, customization options, and how to build effective combined-arms forces.

highlights.label: Mechs
highlights.detail: Scout, brawler, and fire-support frames form the backbone of any drop deck.

highlights.label: Tanks
highlights.detail: Armoured line holders that anchor a push and absorb return fire.

highlights.label: Infantry
highlights.detail: Cheap bodies for flank insertion, objective holds, and emergency reinforcement.

highlights.label: VTOLs
highlights.detail: Fast air units for scouting, harassment, and punishing overextended enemies.

highlights.label: Dropships
highlights.detail: Transports that carry the payload in and are lost with everything inside if the zone is contested.

highlights.label: Factions
highlights.detail: Vanguard, Support, Recon, Heavy, and Swarm rosters that shape your deployment rhythm.

modules.name: Drop Command Mech Builds
modules.description: A build-focused section featuring recommended mech loadouts, weapon choices, equipment setups, and combat strategies. Players can learn how to optimize different playstyles for various missions.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: Mobility-first chassis that repositions the moment it lands and never fights as a static target.

highlights.label: A
highlights.detail: Heat and ammo endurance, so the mech can fight immediately on arrival.

highlights.label: B
highlights.detail: Range coverage that avoids dropping three units built for the same engagement distance.

highlights.label: C
highlights.detail: Cheap replaceable frames that keep your drop cadence alive while the expensive metal is repaired.

modules.name: Drop Command Campaign Guide
modules.description: This module explains the procedural campaign system, planetary conquest, resources, diplomacy, and long-term strategic decisions. It helps players understand how individual battles affect the larger war.

highlights.label: Recon
highlights.detail: Locate enemies and map two approach lanes while saving every drop slot you can.

highlights.label: Insert
highlights.detail: Call one reinforcement or transport to get your squad grouped and armed on the map.

highlights.label: Secure
highlights.detail: Take the objective, then drop supplies once ammo or health starts to dip.

highlights.label: Sustain
highlights.detail: Absorb the enemy response with a second supply or armour drop instead of retreating.

highlights.label: Push
highlights.detail: Convert the hold into a win with an equipment pod or vehicle drop.

highlights.label: Extract
highlights.detail: Leave with what you earned behind smoke, cover, or a distraction drop.

modules.name: Drop Command Missions Guide
modules.description: A mission database explaining objectives, tactical approaches, defensive operations, and attack scenarios. Players can find strategies for completing different battlefield challenges efficiently.

highlights.label: Reinforce
highlights.detail: Add bodies to a push or hold a point, but only when you have cover to receive them.

highlights.label: Supply
highlights.detail: Restore ammo and consumables between fights rather than during them.

highlights.label: Vehicle
highlights.detail: Change the tools available when enemy armour or a fortified position appears.

highlights.label: Medical
highlights.detail: Recover wounded or reset a losing fight while you still control the landing zone.

highlights.label: Defensive
highlights.detail: Deploy barriers, turrets, or mines ahead of an expected counterattack.

highlights.label: Strike
highlights.detail: Deliver area damage from above when enemies are clustered and static.

modules.name: Drop Command Controls Guide
modules.description: A reference guide for keyboard controls, movement systems, combat commands, and gameplay settings. It helps new players quickly learn how to pilot units and manage battles.

highlights.label: Single Key
highlights.detail: One dedicated key drops the selected item: fast for weight dumps, but easy to misfire.

highlights.label: Mod + Key
highlights.detail: Hold a modifier before pressing: good for crowded hotbars, slower in a panic.

highlights.label: Hold
highlights.detail: Press and hold until the command registers to protect rare gear from accidental drops.

highlights.label: Confirm
highlights.detail: A confirmation prompt guards high-value drops but breaks combat flow.

highlights.label: Bind Apart
highlights.detail: Keep drop and destroy on separate keys, since shared binds are the top cause of lost gear.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about Drop Command deployment, timing, and progression.

items.question: What is Drop Command?
items.answer: Drop Command is a tactical sci-fi strategy game about off-map deployment. You spend a limited tonnage budget and a cooldown to call mechs, tanks, infantry, VTOLs, and battle armour onto a landing zone you choose, then use that arrival to break a stalemate or re-anchor a collapsing line.

items.question: How does a drop command actually work in Drop Command?
items.answer: A drop command has four parts: a call-in cost, a delay timer, a landing point, and a payload. The delay decides most fights, because a payload that lands after the engagement is over costs the resource and gains nothing.

items.question: Which faction should beginners pick in Drop Command?
items.answer: Vanguard is the easiest faction to feel productive with because it pressures early, but it fades without follow-up. For a safer first pick, Support or Heavy gives your team a role that stays useful in the mid-game.

items.question: How much tonnage should I keep in reserve in Drop Command?
items.answer: A common rule is to hold roughly a third of your Drop Command allowance for the late game. Emptying the budget on one assault-class arrival leaves you with no answer when the enemy counter-pushes.

items.question: Where can I find Drop Command patch notes?
items.answer: The Drop Command Updates module tracks the dev log, including permission changes, cooldown adjustments, and item-table fixes, with a summary of what changed and where to report problems.
